title: Expanded safe classroom experiment pack
scope: Supplementary teacher-facing experiments for the virtual chemistry lab. This pack keeps to low-risk, classroom-friendly concepts and uses only observation-level descriptions.
virtual_only_notice: Every entry below describes the virtual lab only. It is not a real-world laboratory procedure.

experiments.title: Solution vs. mixture
experiments.focus: Recognize when a solid disperses into a homogeneous solution and when a material remains a separate visible phase.
observations: A dissolved solid becomes invisible as individual crystals.
An insoluble solid remains visible and can be separated conceptually.
Students can compare a mixture with a solution.

experiments.title: Changes of state
experiments.focus: Connect heating and cooling with evaporation, boiling and condensation as physical changes.
observations: Heating increases temperature until boiling can be discussed.
Cooling is presented as the reverse of heating ideas.
The material stays water throughout the physical change.

experiments.title: Saturation and evaporation
experiments.focus: Show that a solution can reach a limit and that removing solvent can reveal dissolved material again.
observations: Concentration increases as solvent is reduced.
A saturated state means the solution has reached its visible classroom limit.
A dissolved solid can reappear when the solution becomes concentrated enough.

experiments.title: Solution formation
experiments.focus: Use particle language to explain why a dissolved substance is still present even when it cannot be seen.
observations: The liquid becomes visually uniform.
The solvent and solute can be named separately.
Different solutes can be compared at a conceptual level.

experiments.title: Filtration concept
experiments.focus: Separate an insoluble solid from a liquid in a classroom-friendly way.
observations: The insoluble solid stays separate from the liquid phase.
Students can compare the idea of a residue with a clear filtrate.
The activity stays at the observation level only.

experiments.title: Paper chromatography concept
experiments.focus: Show that a colour mixture can separate into different bands or spots.
observations: A mixed colour can split into more than one visible component.
Not every component moves in the same way.
Students see a separation idea rather than a real laboratory protocol.

experiments.title: Indicator colour change
experiments.focus: Introduce an indicator as a visual way to compare solutions.
observations: A colour shift can represent a different solution environment.
The activity is about observation and comparison, not procedure.
Students can relate a visible change to acid-base ideas at a high level.

experiments.title: Slow oxidation and rusting
experiments.focus: Explain a gradual chemical change using a familiar metal sample.
observations: A visible change can happen slowly over time.
Students discuss oxygen, moisture and gradual change as a concept.
The model distinguishes a slow chemical change from a fast one.

experiments.title: Model limits and data quality
experiments.focus: Teach students how to judge what the virtual lab does and does not represent.
observations: A model can be useful even when it is simplified.
Not every numerical value should be treated as a measured lab value.
Students can identify assumptions and limitations.

experiments.title: Pathway review and lesson selection
experiments.focus: Confirm the student pathway before choosing chemistry lessons in the lab.
observations: Teacher Mode should start by confirming the pathway.
The same virtual lab can support different lesson choices.
Students can compare a model with the actual official book path.
